verdict.line: You lose this lane getting Disdain-slammed into Purge range before level 6, and win it by level 9+ once Counter Strike eats his Purge channel and Trinity Force comes online.

brief.thesis: Urgot has no mobility except E (Disdain), so once he commits that cooldown to engage he is stuck in melee range with nothing but auto-attacks and Purge. Jax's entire game plan is baiting that E, surviving the Purge window with E (Counter Strike), and punishing the 14-16s lockout. The 48% head-to-head over 1074 games reflects a genuinely even lane where the outcome hinges on who blinks first on cooldowns, not a structural favorite either way.

theirWindow.when: after he lands Disdain on you
theirWindow.what: He's shielded and now in melee range to unload W (Purge), which slows him but deals heavy sustained damage and triggers Echoing Flames blasts. If your E (Counter Strike) is down, you're eating the full Purge channel with no answer.

yourWindow.when: the moment his E (Disdain) is on cooldown (14-16s)
yourWindow.what: He has zero gap-close and zero escape. Walk up and force trades with Q (Leap Strike) into W (Empower) autos — he can't disengage and his only answer is kiting with autos, which you win if your E (Counter Strike) is up to eat his Purge.

start.why: Urgot's Corrosive Charge poke and autos chip you down before you're in melee range; the shield's passive sustain offsets that at a 37.2% pick rate, slightly behind Doran's Blade's 44.7% win rate but safer against a poke-heavy ranged laner.

boots.why: Urgot's damage is entirely physical autos and Purge ticks — Steelcaps (48.8% win rate, 78.6% pick) directly reduces both, far better than Mercury's Treads here since he has no hard CC to dodge.

core.why: The Sheen-empowered auto after Q (Leap Strike) is your primary damage spike in trades and lets you actually threaten him once Disdain is down.
Its on-hit proc and healing let you win extended auto trades during his Purge channel, which is exactly when you need the sustain most.
68.6% win rate over 51 games on this path — the damage-over-time conversion smooths out Purge's burst and Echoing Flames ticks so you don't get deleted mid-trade.

situational.when: he's fed or hitting Fear Beyond Death executes reliably
he's building tank items and you need the shred and sustain over raw burst

runes.keystoneWhy: Taken in the 45.7% page at 31.5% pick — the ramping attack speed turns every post-Disdain trade window into a sustained DPS check that favors Relentless Assault's third-hit bonus damage.

summoners.why: Flash+Teleport is run at 26.5% pick with a 49.7% win rate, the best of the three listed combos here — Teleport lets you reset after losing early trades to poke and still scale into your level 9+ power spike without falling behind on CS.

playing.title: Bait Disdain before trading
playing.detail: Don't engage into his E (Disdain) — let him commit it into melee range first, since it's his only gap-close with a 14-16s cooldown and he's helpless without it.

playing.title: Save E for his Purge channel
playing.detail: Hold Counter Strike (E) until he's already channeling W (Purge) at close range; the attack-dodge window matters most then, matching OP.GG's own read on this matchup.

playing.title: Leap Strike only after Disdain is down
playing.detail: Q (Leap Strike) into his position is only safe once you've tracked his E on cooldown — leaping in before that just walks you into a free Disdain punish.

playing.title: Respect level 6 all-ins
playing.detail: Fear Beyond Death threatens real damage from range starting level 6; don't overextend past minion lines once he hits that level until you have Trinity Force online.

playing.title: Trade in extended fights, not pokes
playing.detail: Jax loses single-auto exchanges to his ranged kit but wins anything that goes past 3-4 seconds thanks to Relentless Assault (R) stacking and Empower (W) burst.

playing.title: Track Purge cooldown post-6
playing.detail: At max rank Purge drops to a 0s cooldown, meaning he can chain it repeatedly in extended fights — don't assume one dodged Purge means you're safe for the rest of the trade.

brief.patchCaveat: Build paths, runes, summoners, and win rates above are measured from live OP.GG game data on the current patch (16.19.1); the mechanical reasoning and timing calls are this brief's own analysis.

stats.opponentTip: Be careful of Urgot closing in with Disdain (E). Be careful of his Purge (W) when he closes in! Use Counter Strike [E] to block his Purge (W).
